That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

title: Optional input reset on re-render
description:
Hi,

When #828  was addressed, the default behaviour for updating the `input` object was changed. Unfortunately the new defaults are incompatible with one of my apps.

In the app I had a few tables where making a selection in one table would update the other tables. With the later versions of DT (post #828) this would then update `input` which triggered an observer and consequently update also the original table where the selection was made (which I did not want to happen). With a pre #828 version of the package the `input` would not be updated, so the original table would not be re-rendered.

So, ideally an option indicating whether or not the input object needs to be updated on re-render would solve my problem and allow me to update the package to the latest version.

title: DT's stopPropagation() of clicked anchor tags in cells; why?
description:
Hi, I'm curious about why [this `stopPropagation`](https://github.com/rstudio/DT/blob/c79c1b328c5d48d0b37024ba1704fc54c94d9ae6/inst/htmlwidgets/datatables.js#L1292) is in place for clicked anchors within a DT cell. I stumbled upon this because I'd registered an anchor-click handler on my DT instance, but found the callback was never being executed.

Solving the problem of my callback not running was easy (i.e. I simply added a NOP class to my anchor tags) once I found this conditional code block, but I can't quite figure out why it's there at all. If a developer wanted to suppress the browser's navigating behavior, for example, one might want to register a `preventDefault` callback. In my particular case, the anchor-click callback triggered an image 'lightbox' presentation (of the `href`-ed image/media file).

My only guess of why this is here might be to suppress Shiny's corresponding `input$tableId_cells_selected`, but why specifically on unclassed anchor tags?

title: How can I create a reactive table based on checkbox inputs?
description:
Reposting from [SO](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/67064821/how-can-i-create-a-reactive-table-based-on-checkbox-inputs) (no response in > 24 hours). I would like to create a Shiny app which displays two tables. The first shows all the data, the second should show a subset of data. The user should be able to choose with rows to exclude from the first table via checkboxes, as well as documenting a reason for their exclusion text input. Yes, it should be a checkbox column rather than using the in-built DT rows_selected functionally.

Additionally, previously "excluded" rows (eventually read from a file) should also  be included in the exclusion list. This would get read in on app launch.

Based on adapting, [this](https://github.com/rstudio/DT/issues/93), I have got some of the way there. But I am not sure how to keep the second table updated based on the interactive checkbox inputs (i.e the new exclusions added at runtime). How could I do this?

```r
    library(shiny)
    library(DT)
    
    # references 
    # https://yihui.shinyapps.io/DT-radio/
    
    shinyInputCheckboxes <- function(FUN, len, id, disqualifiedIDs, ...) {
        # adapted from more general shinyInput function, not most efficient
        inputs <- character(len)
        for (i in seq_len(len)) {
            if(i %in% disqualifiedIDs) {
                inputs[i] <- as.character(FUN(paste0(id, i), label = NULL, value = TRUE, ...))
            }
            else {
                inputs[i] <- as.character(FUN(paste0(id, i), label = NULL, value = FALSE, ...))
            }
        }
        inputs
    }
    
    shinyInputText <- function(FUN, len, id, disqualifiedIDs, disqualified_trials, ...) {
        # adapted from more general shinyInput function, not most efficient
        inputs <- character(len)

    )

        mainStart <- data.frame(ID = 1:10, 
                                exclude = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE), 
                                exclusion_reason = LETTERS[11:20]
                                )
        
        disqualified_trials_ids <- which(mainStart$exclude)
        
        # render a bunch of input fields
        exclude <- shinyInputCheckboxes(checkboxInput, nrow(mainStart), 'exclude_', disqualified_trials_ids)
        exclusion_reason <- shinyInputText(textInput, nrow(mainStart), 'exclusion_reason_', disqualified_trials_ids, mainStart)
        
        main <- mainStart
        main$exclude <- exclude
        main$exclusion_reason <- exclusion_reason
        
        # render the main table of all data
        output$main <- renderDataTable({ main }, server = FALSE, escape = FALSE, selection = 'single', options = list(
            preDrawCallback = JS('function() { Shiny.unbindAll(this.api().table().node()); }'),
            drawCallback = JS('function() { Shiny.bindAll(this.api().table().node()); } ')))
        
        # render the subset table
        output$sub <- renderTable({ 
            mainStart[disqualified_trials_ids, ]
        })
    
    }
    
    
    shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

title: Page across columns
description:
I'd like to make a feature request for the `datatable()` function to allow paging across columns. I often present data and wide tables that do not fit in the width of the page. By default, the `DT` package creates tables that allow the user to page across the rows. However, it does not let the user page across the columns. `DT` allows horizontal scrolling using the following syntax:

```
DT::datatable(data, options = list(scrollX = TRUE))
```

However, I'd prefer to be able to page across columns instead of horizontal scrolling because IMO it is more esthetically simple and easy to use. For this reason, I have preferred to use the `paged_table()` function from the `rmarkdown` package, which pages across rows and columns by default. But I'd like to be able to do this in `DT` because it has some important features that `paged_table()` does not have, such as the ability to search the table contents.

title: Use DataTables smart search on certain columns
description:
I want to apply DataTables "smart" search to specific columns, not all columns. Is this functionality possible with R's `DT` package? Is there a way to add JavaScript that'll get the job done? I'm doing this all in a Shiny app. [StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/66803539/use-datatables-smart-search-on-certain-columns-using-rs-dt-package) and [RStudio Community](https://community.rstudio.com/t/use-datatables-smart-search-on-certain-columns-using-rs-dt-package/100053) could not answer.

I believe I want something similar to the [`columns().search()`](https://datatables.net/reference/api/columns().search()) method in the DataTables library.

Here's a normal global search of all columns:

```r
library(DT)
library(shiny)
library(shinyWidgets)

dat = data.frame(
  first  = letters[1:3],
  second = letters[4:6],
  third  = letters[7:9]
)
ui = function(request) {
  shiny::fluidPage(
    shiny::sidebarLayout(
      shiny::sidebarPanel(
        shinyWidgets::searchInput(
          inputId = "search_all",
          label = "Search all columns"
        )
      ),
      shiny::mainPanel(DT::dataTableOutput("dt"))
    )
  )
}
server = function(input, output, session) {
  output$dt = DT::renderDataTable({
    dat %>%
      DT::datatable(
        options = list(
          dom = "lrtip",
          search = list(search = input$search_all),
          searchHighlight = TRUE
        )
      )
  })
}
shiny::shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Here's what I wish I could do, set target columns for each search input (this doesn't work, I'm just including it for illustration):

```r
library(DT)
library(shiny)
library(shinyWidgets)

dat = data.frame(
  first  = letters[1:3],
  second = letters[4:6],
  third  = letters[7:9]

    shiny::sidebarLayout(

        ),

          inputId = "search_2",
          label = "Search 2 columns"
        )
      ),
      shiny::mainPanel(DT::dataTableOutput("dt"))
    )
  )
}
server = function(input, output, session) {
  output$dt = DT::renderDataTable({
    dat %>%
      DT::datatable(
        options = list(
          dom = "lrtip",
          search = list(
            list(
              targets = c("first"),
              search = input$search_1
            ),
            list(
              targets = c("second", "third"),
              search = input$search_2
            )
          ),
          searchHighlight = TRUE
        )
      )
  })
}
shiny::shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: Custom search function
description:
(Apologies if this has already been asked (I searched through SO and GitHub Issues, but couldn't find anything with this specific question/request))

Is there any mechanism for server-side-processed tables to register one's own search function? I've implemented this _sort of_ already in a Shiny app by using a separate `textInput`, using my own search method on some source data, then row-restricting the server-side DT data and updating my DT via `dataTableProxy` and `replaceData`.

All of this works, but I'd _also_ like to use a few column-specific filters (of factors, so via selectizes). This causes difficulty though, as I now I have this exogenous search method combined with a separate DT-managed row filter. It led me to think that perhaps I can simply replace DT's search implementation with a custom function, provided DT's server-side searching and filtering follow some consistent API (e.g. search functions that return a logical vector of length == number of rows in data, or something similar).

Is this possible? It'd be the equivalent of registering a custom search function (callback) for client-side DataTables, but specifically here registering an _R_ function for server-side processing.

title: Saving changes when editing multiple cells in a DataTable / documentation
description:
When editing a single cell (`editable = "cell"`) I can press `Enter` to save the changes to the table.

When editing multiple cells (`editable = "all"`), I have to press `CTRL+Enter` to save the changes. I found this out by accident after half an hour of trying to save edits in a datatable. It seems this behaviour is not documented anywhere.

My question/request:
* Can this be changed to just require `Enter` (maybe via an option?)
* Can this be added to the documentation of the `edit` argument of  `?datatable`

The behaviour occurs in the latest DT version from gitub (`0.17.2`) as well as the latest CRAN version

title: Issues with extensions scroller + colreorder
description:
I have the following code in my modularized Shiny app and I think that the extensions scroller and colReorder are interfering with each other and thus I cannot set the column widths.  I was digging through other issues throughout this repo and it seems that this is a known issue, but no one had my specific example listed yet, so I'm posting this as documentation for you.

The issue I have is that with the below code, I still have columns that are incredibly wide even though I set the column width to 150px ... I found other issues that stated you needed to have autoWidth = TRUE an scrollX = TRUE in your options to get the column widths to do what you want ... so I've added those and still the columns are obscenely wide...

With these other issues [here](https://github.com/rstudio/DT/issues/895), I'm left to assume it has something to do with the extensions :(

```
DT::datatable(
    data = rawdata_withlinks(),
    rownames = F,
    escape = F,
    filter = 'top',
    extensions = list("ColReorder" = NULL,"Scroller" = NULL),
    callback = JS("table.on('column-reorder', function(e, settings, details){",
                  "  Shiny.setInputValue('colOrder', details.mapping);",
                  "});"), # save order of columns

      scrollX = TRUE,
      autoWidth = TRUE,

      stateSave = TRUE,

title: Remove the js/css files of unsupported themes
description:
datatables library supports lots of themes but DT only supports **three** of them: default, bootstrap3 and bootstrap4.

However, we include all the theme files, which I don't think any user will actually use. So, we should delete those js/css files to shrink the size of the package. In addition, we should tweak the code in `update_DT.R` to exclude those unsupported theme files.

```r
files <- list.files(recursive = TRUE, pattern = "[.](js|css)$")
files <- grep("semanticui|jqueryui|foundation", files, value = TRUE)
size <- sum(file.size(files))
class(size) <- "object_size"
print(size, unit = "KB")
## 129.7 Kb
```

title: addRow without resetting active page and scrolling
description:
It would be nice to be able to add a row without:
1) active page resetting to page 1. 
2) scrolling resetting

To see issue 1 you can go to another page on https://yihui.shinyapps.io/DT-proxy/ and then add a row. --> you are send to page 1 instead of staying where you are

For issue two you can use the following slightly modified example. If you scroll how and then add a row it would be nice to stay where you were with the scroll.

```r
library(shiny)
library(DT)

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  # using server = FALSE mainly for addRow(); server = TRUE works for
  # selectRows() and selectColumns()
  output$foo = DT::renderDataTable(
    iris, server = FALSE, selection = list(target = 'row+column'),
    caption = 'Using a proxy object to manipulate the table',
    options = list(pageLength=-1,
                               scrollY = "200px",
                               bPaginate = FALSE)
  )

  proxy = dataTableProxy('foo')

  observeEvent(input$select1, {
    proxy %>% selectRows(as.numeric(input$rows))
  })

  observeEvent(input$select2, {
    proxy %>% selectColumns(input$col)
  })

  observeEvent(input$clear1, {
    proxy %>% selectRows(NULL)
  })

  observeEvent(input$clear2, {
    proxy %>% selectColumns(NULL)
  })

  observeEvent(input$add, {
    proxy %>% addRow(iris[sample(nrow(iris), 1), , drop = FALSE])
  })

  observe({
    if (input$cap != '') proxy %>% updateCaption(input$cap)
  })

  output$info = renderPrint({
    list(rows = input$foo_rows_selected, columns = input$foo_columns_selected)
  })

})



library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(

  title = 'Manipulate an Existing Table',

  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectizeInput('rows', 'Row IDs', choices = seq_len(nrow(iris)), multiple = TRUE),
      actionButton('select1', 'Select Rows'),

description:
I have also posted this issue in the Docker community: https://forums.docker.com/t/r-shiny-datatables-giving-ajax-error-using-docker-swarm/98020

I’ve set up a Docker swarm on a single machine with 5 replicas containing an R Shiny application (docker-compose.yml copied below).

On visiting the site and attempting to display a datatable, I get the following error:

DataTables warning: table id=DataTables_Table_1 - Ajax error. For more information about this error, please see http://datatables.net/tn/7

This only occurs when using Docker swarm. When I manually run the shiny app from within a running Docker container (created from the same image as used for the Docker swarm) the datatable displays as expected without error.

I’ve reinstalled htmlwidgets, DT and jsonlite packages from source using the devtools package.

Apart from the issue with the datatable the app runs fine. Example of code for outputting table from Shiny app.R:

    output$di_infra = DT::renderDataTable({
    dt_table(di_dt)
    })

If I add server = FALSE to the above function then the tables will display, but the response is very slow as the processing is not done on the server.

I guess the problem may relate to the configuration of my docker-compose.yml file or a bug?

My docker-compose.yml file:

    version: "3.7"
    services:

       image: docker_image_name
       deploy:
          replicas: 5

title: StyleColorBar issue (webkit): value > upper range
description:
Hi all,

on iOS the linear gradient style (created by StyleColorBar) is not displayed if the value of the cell is greater than the upper limit.
(=> CSS percentage is <= 0 which is a problem for webkit)

I suggest to add Math.max:
https://github.com/rstudio/DT/blob/bbe64749397914a3eaf59dc5f9f0d4ab34f301cb/R/format.R#L392-L393

```r
JS(sprintf(
    "isNaN(parseFloat(value)) || value <= %f ? '' : 'linear-gradient(%fdeg, transparent ' + Math.max(%f - value,0)/%f * 100 + '%%, %s ' + Math.max(%f - value,0)/%f * 100 + '%%)'",
    r1, angle, r2, r, color, r2, r
  ))
```

Best regards

title: Style choices get lost with `if` rule in `renderDataTable()` (Shiny)
description:
Hi everyone,

I just noticed a strange behavior, possibly a (minor) bug. It seems that having an `if` rule within `renderDataTable()`, can make the table forget the style that was applied to it.

**Reprex**

```r
library(shiny)
library(DT)
library(shinyWidgets)

data(iris)

ui <- fluidPage(
    tagList(
        shinyWidgets::materialSwitch(
                inputId = "switch",
                label = "Show table:",
                value = TRUE,
                inline = TRUE
        ),
        uiOutput("content")
    )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
    output[["content"]] <- renderUI({
        if ( input[["switch"]] == TRUE ) {
            dataTableOutput("table")
        } else {
            textOutput("no_data")
        }
    })
    output[["table"]] <- renderDataTable({
        if ( input[["switch"]] == TRUE ) {
            DT::datatable(
                iris,
                autoHideNavigation = TRUE,
                class = "stripe table-bordered table-condensed",
                escape = FALSE,
                filter = list(position = "top", clear = TRUE),
                rownames = FALSE,
                selection = "single",
                style = "bootstrap",
                options = list(
                    dom = "frtlip",
                    pageLength = 10,
                    scrollX = TRUE
                )
            )
        }
    })
    output[["no_data"]] <- renderText("No data.")
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

There is a button that controls whether the table (that uses the `bootstrap` style) or an alternative message is shown. Now, in this example, even though not reflecting any realistic setting, I have also added an `if` rule that, again, checks the status of the switch. When the app is launched, the table is shown with the correct style (see screenshot below).

![Screen Shot 2020-08-03 at 15 11 52](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18103560/89186257-ce89b580-d59b-11ea-8419-56f0c6e3d62c.png)

However, after using the switch to display the alternative message, and then switching back to the table, the table is shown again, however without the `bootstrap` style (see screenshot).

![Screen Shot 2020-08-03 at 15 12 03](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18103560/89186268-d34e6980-d59b-11ea-9ae4-40d34c1426b9.png)

When looking at the HTML code, I noticed that the `dt-bootstrap` is missing in the list of classes of the respective `div` container.

Before using the switch:
![Screen Shot 2020-08-03 at 15 12 40](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18103560/89186312-e5c8a300-d59b-11ea-8470-f06e7db837b8.png)

After using the switch:
![Screen Shot 2020-08-03 at 15 12 27](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18103560/89186303-e2cdb280-d59b-11ea-94b0-faf43275f14b.png)

**Workaround**

In my actual scenario, I used the `if` statement to make some format checks on the input data. The workaround is to move those checks from the `renderDataTable()` call to the `renderUI()` call. In my case, that was no problem, but it might be inconvenient in other scenarios. That's why I decided to report this behavior here.

If you think this is important enough, maybe somebody could have a look at what's going on here.

Thank you!

title: DT::formatRound raises an error if argument `columns` has names

```r
data <- mtcars

  vapply(colnames(data),
         function(x) is.double(data[[x]]) &&
           ! inherits(data[[x]], "integer64"),

The first `DT::formatRound` raises the rather obscure error "'options' must be a fully named list, or have no names (NULL)".  The second command works.

This probably also concerns similar functions from `DT`.

title: When using the Select extension, _rows_selected is not reset when the table is rerendered
description:
## Problem Description

In a shiny app that includes a table created using DT, the object `input$table_rows_selected` is not reset to `NULL` after the table is rerendered. This happens only, when the "Select" extension is used, but not with the built-in selection mechanism. The issue appears independent of the value of the option `select.style`.

The object `input$table_cell_clicked` is reset to an empty list in both cases.

I am not entirely sure that this is a bug since I have not found any statement what the expected behaviour for the Select extension is. However, given that is different for the built-in mechanism and the extension and that `input$table_cell_clicked` is reset in both cases, it is at least counter-intuitive.


## Session Info

I use the newest stable versions of R and RStudio, have updated all packages and installed `DT` from github.
This is the output of `xfun::session_info('DT')`:

```
R version 4.0.2 (2020-06-22)
Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit)
Running under: Ubuntu 18.04.4 LTS, RStudio 1.3.1056

Locale:
  LC_CTYPE=en_GB.UTF-8       LC_NUMERIC=C               LC_TIME=de_CH.UTF-8       
  LC_COLLATE=en_GB.UTF-8     LC_MONETARY=de_CH.UTF-8    LC_MESSAGES=en_GB.UTF-8   
  LC_PAPER=de_CH.UTF-8       LC_NAME=C                  LC_ADDRESS=C              
  LC_TELEPHONE=C             LC_MEASUREMENT=de_CH.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C       

Package version:
  base64enc_0.1.3   BH_1.72.0.3       crosstalk_1.1.0.1 digest_0.6.25    
  DT_0.14.1         graphics_4.0.2    grDevices_4.0.2   htmltools_0.5.0  
  htmlwidgets_1.5.1 jsonlite_1.7.0    later_1.1.0.1     lazyeval_0.2.2   
  magrittr_1.5      methods_4.0.2     promises_1.1.1    R6_2.4.1         
  Rcpp_1.0.5        rlang_0.4.7       stats_4.0.2       utils_4.0.2      
  yaml_2.2.1  
```

## Minimal Reproducible Example

The following app demonstrates the problem. There is a button that forces rerendering of the table and a selection input that can be used to toggle between the built-in selection and the extension. Under the table, the values of `input$table_rows_selected` and `input$table_cell_clicked` are shown.

The issue can be reproduced by selecting one or more rows and then clicking "Reload". `input$table_rows_selected` remains unchanged, while `input$table_cell_clicked` is reset to an empty list.

When "Select Type" is set to "built-in", also `input$table_rows_selected` is reset to `NULL` when reloading.

```r
library(shiny)
library(DT)

ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("reload", "Reload"),
  selectInput("select_type", "Select Type",
              c("extension", "built-in")),
  radioButtons('type', NULL, c("row", 'column', 'cell')),
  DTOutput("table"),
  textOutput("rowselected"),
  textOutput("colselected"),
  textOutput("cellselected"),
  textOutput("clicked")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  output$table <- renderDT({
    input$reload
    if (input$select_type == "built-in") {
      datatable(mtcars[1:5, ], selection = list(target = input$type))
    } else {
      datatable(mtcars[1:5, ],
                extensions = "Select",
                selection = "none",
                options = list(
                  select = list(style = "multi", items = input$type)
                )
      )
    }},
    server = FALSE
  )
  
  output$rowselected <- renderPrint(
    input$table_rows_selected
  )
  output$colselected <- renderPrint(
    input$table_columns_selected
  )
  output$cellselected <- renderPrint(
    input$table_cells_selected
  )
  
  output$clicked <- renderPrint(
    input$table_cell_clicked
  )
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: Issue with DT SearchPanes : only first 10 unique values appear in the panes
description:
Hi there, 

I am trying to use the new SearchPanes and Buttons features from the DT package for filtering/selecting rows of a (rather large) datatable within a shiny app, along with the Scroller extension but I have problems with the searchpanes: when using both SearchPanes and Scroller only the first 10 unique values appear in the searchpanes.

Minimal example with the dataset gapminder form package gapminder:

```
library(shiny)
library(DT)
library(magrittr)
library(gapminder)

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    dataTableOutput('tbl')
  ),

  server = function(input, output) {
    output$tbl = renderDataTable(server=FALSE, {
      datatable(gapminder,
        rownames = FALSE,
        colnames = c("Country", "Continent", "Year",
                     "Life Exp", "Population", "GDP per capita"),
        extensions = c("SearchPanes", "Select", "Buttons", "Scroller"),
        options = list(
          dom = "Brtip",
          buttons = list("searchPanes"),
          language = list(searchPanes = list(collapse = "Filter Rows")),
          scrollY = 500,
          scroller = TRUE,
          columnDefs = list(
            list(searchPanes = list(show = FALSE), targets = c(3:5)),
            list(searchPanes = list(controls = FALSE), targets = 0:2),
            list(className = "dt-center", targets = 0:5)
          )
        ),
        selection="none"
      ) %>% 
      formatRound(4, 1) %>% 
      formatRound(5, 0) %>%

)

title: Value of `input$foo_cells_selected` when no cell is selected is `<0 x 0 matrix>` instead of `NULL`
description:
When row or column selection is enabled, the value of  `input$foo_rows_selected` or  `input$foo_columns_selected` when no row or column is selected is `NULL`.  When cell selection is enabled, the value of  `input$foo_cells_selected` when no cell is selected is `<0 x 0 matrix>`.

This causes a minor annoyance when I observe the cell selection since I only want to trigger the `observeEvent` when a cell is selected but not when it is deselected.  With row and column selection this isn't an issue since `observeEvent` ignores nulls by default.  But with cell selection, a workaround is needed to check if the length of `input$foo_cells_selected` is greater than 0.

Is it possible to have `input$foo_cells_selected` be `NULL` when no cell is selected, or would changing that create more problems than it resolves?

title: scroll bars do not appear when renderDataTable is used in flexdashboard
description:
Quite possibly a bug - not sure whether in `DT` or `flexdashboard`.

Here's the problem:
I'm rendering a datatable in a shiny flexdashboard app in a reactive context, so that it updates when an input in changed. My dataset isn't large enough to use pagination, so the user should be able to scroll in Y direction to see all records. However, scroll bars do not appear when the table is updated in `renderDataTable`.

This issue has been asked on StackOverflow [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41814311/data-table-output-not-scrollable-in-y-direction) without a satisfactory resolution.

Here's how the problem can be reproduced within a simple shiny flexdashboard Rmd file. In comparison, the scroll bars appear in `renderTable` as expected. Similarly, datatable also works as expected when used in a non-reactive context with a fixed input.

To be sure, I have tried both the current CRAN and development versions of `DT` and `flexdashboard` without success.

``````rmd
---
title: "Test Flexboard Shiny App"
runtime: shiny
output: 
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
    orientation: columns
    vertical_layout: fill
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(flexdashboard)
library(shiny)
library(shinythemes)
library(DT)
library(tidyverse)
```


Sidebar {.sidebar}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
selectInput("data_set", "Pick a dataset", choices = c("mtcars","airquality"), selected = "mtcars")
```

```{r}

# Input dataset
mydataset <- reactive({
  
  name <- input$data_set
  df <- switch(name,
               "mtcars" = mtcars,
               "airquality" = airquality)
  
  return(df)
})
```


Column {data-width=500}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### renderTable (reactive)

```{r}

renderTable(mydataset(), rownames = TRUE)
```


Column {data-width=500}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### renderDataTable (reactive)

```{r}

DT::renderDataTable(datatable(mydataset(), rownames = TRUE,
                              options = list(bPaginate = FALSE, searching = FALSE, info = FALSE)))
```

```{r}

datatable(mtcars, rownames = TRUE, 
          options = list(bPaginate = FALSE, searching = FALSE, info = FALSE))
```

title: `DT:::DT2BSClass` (and perhaps other functions) strips away user classes from `<table>` element
description:
In `datatable()`, any classes the user has added to the `class` argument are stripped away. When the style is `bootstrap`, e.g., the culprit is [`DT:::DT2BSClass()`](https://github.com/rstudio/DT/blob/master/R/datatables.R#L224): ```R > DT:::DT2BSClass("table-condensed foo") [1] "table table-condensed" > DT:::DT2BSClass(c("table-condensed", "foo")) [1] "table table-condensed" ``` Is there any way to allow the caller to add their own class(es) to the resulting `` tag that DT creates/maintains? I'm also happy to spin up a PR to retain any non-recognized classes to the class list, though prior to doing so I just want to check to make sure you don't think this would break anything else :-)

title: Allow the `default` argument of `styleEqual` to reference the column(s) specified in the `valueColumns` argument.
description:
This previously worked but was considered a bug per #799.  It would be useful if we could store css values in column(s) in the table and use those column(s) as the argument to `valueColumns`.  Then in `styleEqual`, use the `valueColumns` columns as the default.

The below code does what is described in v0.13, but not in the latest development version now that the bug has been fixed.

```
df <- data.frame(COL_1 = c("A", "B", "C"),
                     COL_2 = c("D", "E", "F"),
                     COL_1_COLOR = c("#DF9AC2", "#83BF9A", "#A2D485"),
                     COL_2_COLOR = c("#D0DA12", "#0DFFFF", "#A233CD"),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    
    datatable(df) %>% 
      formatStyle(columns = c(1, 2),
                  valueColumns = c(3, 4),
                  target = "cell",
                  background = styleEqual(levels = "",
                                          values = ""))
```

Perhaps this is not the intended use of `styleEqual` and would be better handled by a new separate style function.

title: formatStyle using input data's value, e.g. color definition
description:
I'm not sure whether this is intended behaviour but in years of using DT I haven't come across documentation for this.

What happened to me is: I have a data.table that (unexpectedly) has color definitions in a String column that serves as the value column for DT::formatStyle, as below (**Peru** corresponds to the color #cd853f, which I found out after a painful hour of debugging):

```
library(magrittr)
library(data.table)

dt_iris = iris %>% 
  data.table %>% 
  .[1:5] %>% 
  rbind(data.table(Species = "Peru"), fill = T) %>% 
  rbind(data.table(Species = "blue"), fill = T) %>% 
  rbind(data.table(Species = "#ABCDEF"), fill = T) %>% 
  rbind(data.table(Species = "foo"), fill = T)

dt_iris %>% 
  DT::datatable() %>% 
  DT::formatStyle(
    1,
    "Species",
    "row",
    background = styleEqual2(
      "setosa",
      "red"
    )
  )

```

Which produces the following:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8114107/79166315-2b8f0f00-7de5-11ea-8da2-63084d580039.png)


**update:** The generated html (which has `style="background: peru"` **but not** `style="background: foo"`) as well as the rowCallback which looks correct to me (`"function(row, data) {\nvar value=data[5]; $(row).css({'background':value == \"setosa\" ? \"red\" : value});\n}"`) make me think that there is some JS color recognition logic happening in the datatable package, so it's probably not a DT issue.

Unfortunately I don't know enough JS to be able to debug this.

title: formatting functions don't support vectorized inputs any more
description:
DT 0.13 has introduced a strange bug:

```r
library(magrittr)
Data <- data.frame(Class=LETTERS[1:5], x=runif(5), y=runif(5))
DT::datatable(Data)
DT::datatable(Data) %>% DT::formatRound(2:3, digits=c(2, 2))

title: Modifying POST request payload
description:
## Summary
This line of code will display an error in a user's browser if I modify the request body payload by altering the names used in the POST request. 

```R
    res = tryCatch(filter(data, params), error = function(e) {
      list(error = as.character(e))
    })
```

For context we had this line cause a failure in  - I believe -  pen testing software on the grounds it's leaking the application code. I would argue that but won't here. It feels like the above could be passed back to my R session in the form of an error that I can sanitize when in a Shiny app. Instead of as is, where it's passed to toJSON and displayed as a JSON error.

## Steps to reproduce:
- Using [this example app](https://yihui.shinyapps.io/DT-rows/)
- Modify the request body - in Firefox, right click and 'Inspect Element '
- Select the POST request for the table, begins 'x3?w='
- Click on the 'Edit and Resend' button
- Replace 'searchable' with 'isnotsearchable' or any string other than 'searchable'
- Click on 'Send' and go to the Response tab
- The response will be a JSON error "Error in if (col[["searchable"]] != "true") next: argument is of length zero"
- Note a similar error will result for other named elements used in logical operations in dataTablesFilter, for example: ``` if ((k <- col[['search']][['value']]) == '') next```

title: FR: Only allow proxy selection (while disable users' ability to select)
description:
I suppose it's debatable whether this is a bug or a feature, but it is not possible to select rows using the proxy if datatable(..., selection="none"). 

I would like to only programmatically select rows in a table. I don't want the user to ever select rows interactively. However, if selection="none", then the console reports that selectRows method is not found.  I want the datatables API functionality of [table.select.style("api")](https://datatables.net/reference/api/select.style()).

This is mysterious to me because I can't access the shinyMethods attribute from the console unless I break inside the datatable-calls customMessageHandler in datatables.js. And I also can't see the datatables methods associated with the Select extension. Is the datatable Select extension even used?

None of these work:
```javascript
$("#table1 .dataTable").DataTable().shinyMethods
$("#table1 .dataTable").DataTable().select.style("api")
$("#table1 .dataTable").DataTable().rows().select()
```


Simple example below.
```r

library(shiny)
library(DT)

ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("select_all_1","Select All Rows Table 1"),
  dataTableOutput("table1"),
  actionButton("select_all_2","Select All Rows Table 2"),
  dataTableOutput("table2")
)

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram
server <- function(input, output) {
  table1.proxy <- dataTableProxy("table1")
  table2.proxy <- dataTableProxy("table2")
  observeEvent(input$select_all_1, { 
    selectRows(table1.proxy, 1:3)
  })
  observeEvent(input$select_all_2, { 
    selectRows(table2.proxy, 1:3)
  })
  output$table1 <- renderDT(DT::datatable(data.frame(x=1:3), selection="multiple"))
  output$table2 <- renderDT(DT::datatable(data.frame(y=1:3), selection="none"))
}

# Run the application 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

title: Add possibility to change vertical alignment of tables
description:
The default vertical alignment of centering is not appropriate for all tables (actually, I am wondering if it ever is).  I believe that there is currently no easy way to change the vertical alignment from within the `DT`-package.

For the underlying Javascript library, I found the following:
https://datatables.net/forums/discussion/35586/aligning-cell-contents-vertically
which proposes to use CSS for all of the table.  It would be nicer to have a per-column control, but for my application, changing it for the whole table would be ok.

I would be willing to work on adding this feature to DT.  What would be a good strategy?

1. Is vertical alignment important enough to add an option to `DT::datatable`?
2. Is there an easy way change the CSS-styling of a datatable object?  If yes, maybe it is enough to include an example (to the website or the documentation or the vignette)
3. Would it make sense to add per-column or per-cell styling options to `DT::datatable`?

title: Issue with rendering table using autowidth and scrollX
description:
Table rendering with autowidth and scrollX using R package DT

I am having an issue with rendering of the table using the DT package. The table is generated based on clicked events in a plotly plot. I need the table not to span the entire width if there are not enough columns. So as per the vignette, I added the following code to options in the function datatable from DT package:

```   
     autoWidth = TRUE,
     columnDefs = list(list(className = 'dt-center'
                                         , width = '200px'
                                         , targets = '_all'))
```

This results in the correct display as desired, on the first click as shown in screenshot Auto-Click1.png (See 1st image). However, if I click on any point the second time, the resulting table spans the full width of the browser. (See Auto-Click2.png or the 2nd image). I would like to have the table displayed as in Auto-Click1 and the rendering to persists between clicks.

To keep the width persistent between clicks, I tried to add the option scrollX=TRUE. This helps and the width persists between clicks. But the column headers are now misaligned to the left of the rest of the table. See ScrollX-True.png (See 3rd image).

Here is a complete reproducible example:

```
    ---
    title: "Dashboard with DT and plotly.  Reproducible example"
    output: 
      flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
        orientation: rows
        vertical_layout: fill
    runtime: shiny
    ---

    Dashboard
    ======================

    ```{r setup, include=FALSE}
    library(tidyverse)
    library(tidyselect)
    library(tidyr)
    library(magrittr)
    library(dplyr)
    library(ggplot2)
    library(plotly)
    library(shiny)
    library(shinydashboard)
    library(flexdashboard)
    library(rlang)
    library(DT)
    library(readxl)
    library(writexl)

    ```

    Row 
    -----------------------------------------------------------------------

    ### Plot {.no-padding}

    ```{r}
    data <- mtcars %>%
    rownames_to_column("Model") %>%
    mutate(Make = sub("\\s+.*","", Model))

    ## Plot in the top row
    renderPlotly({
      p <- data %>%
        ggplot(aes(wt, mpg, color = factor(gear))) +
        geom_point() + guides(color=guide_legend("Gear"))
      ggplotly(p,source = "A") %>%
        event_register("plotly_click")
    })
    ```



    Row
    ---------------------------------------


    ### Data Table 

    ```{r tbl}
    renderUI({
      e <- event_data("plotly_click", priority = "event", source = "A")
      chosen_gear <- data %>% 
        pull(gear) %>% 
        unique() %>% 
        sort() %>% 
        .[e[1,"curveNumber"] + 1]

      if(is.null(e))
        return("Click events will appear here")

      DF <- data %>% 
        filter(gear == chosen_gear) %>% 
        dplyr::select(Model, wt, mpg, gear, Make)

      tbl <- DF  %>%
        datatable(rownames = FALSE
                  , extensions = 'Buttons'
                  , options = list(
                    ##scrollX = TRUE, 
                    # Turning the scrollX option on causes Column headers to misalign with rest of the table
                    # Without the scrollX option table has correct width on first click but
                    # On the second click expands to the full width.
                    autoWidth = TRUE
                    , columnDefs = list(list(className = 'dt-center'
                                             , width = '200px'
                                             , targets = '_all'))
                    , dom = "Blrtip"
                    , buttons = list("copy", list(
                      extend = "collection"
                      , buttons = c("csv", "excel", "pdf")
                      , text = "Download"
                    ))
                    , lengthMenu = list(c(5, -1)
                                        , c(5, "All"))
                    , pageLength = 5))

      output$table <- renderDT({tbl})

      DTOutput("table")
    })
```

```

The main issue is that the output is then a non-standard `row x column` table, since it has 2 extra lines at the top:

```

Thus, the user must then either remove these 2 lines prior to importing the table into R (or other software) or modify the import code to skip the first 2 lines. 

I'm guessing that a lot of DT users would like to be able to remove this default behavior and just have the row x column table. However, I don't see anywhere in the docs on how to skip remove the title line. It's obvious how to remove row names or column names from the button export, but what about the title?

title: Citations in datatable
description:
I am working on a bookdown project where we have large tables that also contain citations. We are outputting in both html and pdf.
The problem is that I cannot find a way to make the citations render in the tables. I have also asked on [SO](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/59556135/citations-in-dtdatatable).

For PDF output this latex workaround works if I use kable: https://github.com/haozhu233/kableExtra/issues/214
However, for the html output I have been using `DT:datatable` and I cannot figure a way to make the references render.

Is there a way to get the markdown parsed citation in the table?



markdown example:

    ---
    title: "Untitled"
    output: html_document
    bibliography: ["references.bib"]
    ---
    
    
    In text citation [@chambers_2012].
    
    
    A plan data.frame can render the reference if inserted as text that markdown can parse.
    
    ```{r, results='asis'}
    library(dplyr)
    library(DT)
    
    data_frame(citation = "[@chambers_2012]")
    
    ```
    
    But not in a DT.
    
    ```{r, results='asis'}
    library(dplyr)
    library(DT)
    
    data_frame(citation = "[@chambers_2012]") %>% datatable()
    
    ```
    
    
    
    # bibliography


Sample references.bib

title: Testing editable DT with shinytest
description:
I'm trying to create unit tests for a shiny app I've been working on but can't work out how to input values to an editable DT table.

Example app:
```
library(shiny)
library(DT)

ui <- fluidPage(
  DTOutput("table"), 
  textOutput("mean")
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  tableUpdate <- reactiveVal(0)
  
  table <- data.frame(A = 1:5, B = 6:10, C = 11:15)
  
  output$table <- renderDT({table},
    options = list(paging = FALSE, dom = 't'),
    selection = 'none',
    server = FALSE,
    editable = list(target = 'row')
  )
  
  observeEvent(input$table_cell_edit, {
    table <<- editData(table, input$table_cell_edit)
    tableUpdate(tableUpdate() + 1)
  })
  
  output$mean <- renderText({
    tableUpdate()
    paste(mean(table$A), mean(table$B), mean(table$C))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Example test:
```
library(shinytest)

app <- ShinyDriver$new(".")
app$setInputs(table_cell_clicked = list(row = 2, col = 2, value = 7), allowInputNoBinding_ = TRUE)
app$setInputs(table_cell_edit = data.frame(row = 2, col = 0:3, value = "1"), 
              allowInputNoBinding_ = TRUE, priority_ = "event", wait_ = FALSE, values_ = FALSE)
app$takeScreenshot()
app$stop()
rm(app)
```

I've kept this mostly how it came out when I recorded the test (`recordTest(".")`), but I've corrected the setInputs values of table_cell_edit and table_cell_clicked (which came out as vectors instead of dataframes).

This gives the error:
`Error in sd_getAllValues(self, private, input, output, export) : 
  Unable to fetch all values from server. Is target app running with options(shiny.testmode=TRUE?)`

Running in test mode does not fix the issue.

Have already asked here:

title: Cells are not fully disabled
description:
https://github.com/rstudio/DT/blob/832714f7c928ec8f09d595a7dcd0e9ac9a860254/inst/htmlwidgets/datatables.js#L747

Is there a way to fully disable the cells so that clicking on them does not display them in an edit-like cell? Currently using `editable=list(target='cell', disable=list(columns=c(2)))` results in column 2 being shaded and labeled as 'readonly', but it still is displayed in an edit-like cell and any formatting is lost. 

For example, if a column 2 is disabled but has formatSignif applied then when double-clicked it is redisplayed with full display of digits. Or if the column is not escaped because it contains an HTML icon, the cell is shown with the HTML - even though it's not editable.

Maybe there's a way to truly disable editing so that double clicking on a disabled column does nothing?

title: Using options > language breaks "DT-radio example"
description:
I tried to make a slight change to the example app of @yihui https://yihui.shinyapps.io/DT-radio/ to add the language option **from url** ('//cdn.datatables.net/plug-ins/1.10.11/i18n/French.json') in `renderDataTable`, but the app no longer returned the months radio input.
More details in the related question on SO : https://stackoverflow.com/questions/56780937/r-shiny-dt-with-radio-buttons-breaks-when-adding-language-option
Someone found a trick to make it work by moving the `Shiny.unbindAll` & `Shiny.bindAll` in the `initComplete` script rather that in the `callback`.

Here is the code that doesn't work (simply adding the `language` option)
```
library(shiny)
library(DT)
shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    title = 'Radio buttons in a table',
    DT::dataTableOutput('foo'),
    verbatimTextOutput('sel')
  ),
  server = function(input, output, session) {
    m = matrix(
      as.character(1:5), nrow = 12, ncol = 5, byrow = TRUE,
      dimnames = list(month.abb, LETTERS[1:5])
    )

title: [Feature Request] Access all table cell values by exposing an input$xxx selector (without having to click/select)
description:
I am developing an app where I display a (large) Markov transition matrix as a datatable, rendered client side. Of course, we can make this transition matrix editable for the user. 

I would like to be able to:

- after the user edits some cells and then clicks an update button, 
- to capture all values in all cells of this newly edited datatable (which was edited client side), and return it to R, say, as a matrix

Here is a sample shiny app that might implement this:

```
library(DT)

    fluidPage(
        textOutput('edit'),
        DTOutput('test'),

title: R datatable server-side search option doesn't handle exotic encoding (latin1)
description:
# Context 
I've been trying to develop an R Shiny webapp using DT to display a datatable. I need to use an input to fill the datatable search option as I'm filtering and ordering the possibles search-terms by term-freq. My data is in french, therefore it includes accents with latin1 encoding (I tried UTF8 encoding but the rendering gets messy).

# My attempts
I compared renderDataTable behaviours in server-side computing and client-side computing. The client-side works well, but the data is to large to be handled that way. The server-side finds no match for accentuated terms (french accents).

Here is a repex

```
library(shiny)
library(DT)
data=data.frame(index=1:6,nom=c("hého","bonjour","enchanté","merci","où ça ?","à qui s'adresse-t-il ?"),stringsAsFactors = F)

ui <- fluidPage(
  title = 'Use the DT package in shiny',
  selectizeInput(inputId = 'tag',label="mots pour filtrer",
                 choices=strsplit(data$nom,split = " ")%>%unlist%>%unique),  
  h3('A Table Using Client-side Processing'),
  fluidRow(
    DT::dataTableOutput('tbl_a')
  ),
  h3('A Table Using Server-side Processing'),
  fluidRow(
    DT::dataTableOutput('tbl_b')
  )
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$tbl_a = DT::renderDataTable(datatable(data,options=list(search=list(search=input$tag))), server = FALSE)
  output$tbl_b = DT::renderDataTable(datatable(data,options=list(search=list(search=input$tag))))
}


shinyApp(ui,server)
```

title: Scroller extension fixes row height
description:
Using the scroller plugin fixes the column height in the output, which destroys wrapping.

Edit: Changed examples to use the diamonds dataset

Consider

```
library(magrittr)
library(DT)
library(tidyverse)

diamonds %>%
    slice(1:1000) %>% 
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
        cut =
            rep(cut, 50) %>%
            paste(collapse = " ")
    ) %>%
    datatable(
        options = list(
            deferRender = TRUE,
            searching = TRUE,
            scrollX =  1000,
            scrollY = "45vh"
))
```

Versus

```
library(magrittr)
library(DT)
library(tidyverse)

 diamonds %>%
    slice(1:1000) %>%

    mutate(

            paste(collapse = " ")

datatable(

    options = list(

        searching = TRUE,
        scrollX =  1000,
        scroller = TRUE,
        scrollY = "45vh"
))
```

title: Add dynamic row rank to DT
description:
I am trying to add a row rank from smallest value to largest value in my shiny Data Table based on the order of the rows. I want the row rank to update based on the column that is ordered. My best ideas would either be to use `rownames` but those change with the rows or to use `input$table_state$order` and `saveState` to figure out what column is being ordered and then recalculate a rank column but had no luck. I've included an example using the `iris` dataset.

    library(shiny)
    library(DT)
    library(tidyverse)

     data = iris %>% distinct(Species, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
        arrange(Sepal.Length) %>%
        mutate(rank = 1:3) %>%
        select(rank, Species, everything())


     # Define UI for application that draws a histogram
     ui <- fluidPage(
      DT::dataTableOutput("table")
    )

    # Define server logic required to draw a histogram
    server <- function(input, output) {
     output$table = DT::renderDataTable({
     DT::datatable(data,
              rownames = FALSE,
              options = list(
                columnDefs = list(list(orderable = FALSE, targets = 0:1)),
                order = list(list(2, "asc")),
                ordering = TRUE
              ))
    })

    }

    # Run the application

title: Filter headers jump sideways and become unusable when there is a horizontal scrollbar
description:
When using filters positioned on top of the table, and the table is wide enough for the horizontal scrollbar to appear, the right-most filters -- esp. numeric and factor -- become unusable. 

Here's a minimal example: 

    ---
    title: "MRE"
    author: ""
    output: 
      flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
        orientation: columns
        vertical_layout: fill
    runtime: shiny
    ---
    
    Page 1 {data-orientation=columns}
    =======================================================================
    
    Column {data-width=650}
    -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    ### Tab 1
    
    ```{r}
    require(dplyr)
    DT::renderDataTable({  
        ##BUG: trying to activate the last 2 filters (factor and numeric) will trigger UI artefacts
        DT::datatable(mtcars %>% 
                          mutate(am = as.character(am), 
                                 gear = as.factor(gear)), 
                      
                      filter = 'top',
                      extensions = c('Scroller'),
                      options = list(scrollY=600, 
                                     scrollX=300, 
                                     scroller = TRUE,
                                     deferRender = TRUE,
                                     pageLength = 250), fillContainer = TRUE)
    })  
    
    ```
    
    Column {data-width=650}
    -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    ### Tab 2
    
If you activate the first few filters, they behave as expected (e.g. the filter for `disp`). And things seem to work fine if you activate the `character` filter (i.e. for `am`). 
![screenshot_2018-09-29_11-09-35](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1318567/46249123-bf061800-c3d8-11e8-845d-b382e52886de.png)


But things get weird when you activate the `factor` filter, for `gear`. As soon as you click in the box, the table will "visually" disappear. It's just an artefact, by the looks of it, as after you select a level and click 'elsewhere', the table is rendered again. Even so, the behavior is a bit awkward. 
![screenshot_2018-09-29_11-09-43](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1318567/46249140-48b5e580-c3d9-11e8-930a-108e4c6a6d61.png)


Unfortunately the `numeric` filters simply become unusable. Unactivated the filters display as expected: 
![screenshot_2018-09-29_11-25-00](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1318567/46249223-561f9f80-c3da-11e8-98b8-1768e25ff57d.png)

If you activate the filter for e.g. `carb`, then all the headers jump sideways way to the left: 
![screenshot_2018-09-29_11-19-41](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1318567/46249231-7d766c80-c3da-11e8-9001-629083ec51f4.png)

At that moment the `slider` is invisible to the user, and the artefact makes the UI confusing. Resizing the window doesn't seem to help. The only thing that does something is hitting `ESC`, which will then display the slider (although, like for `factor` filters, the table itself will become hidden). And unfortunately this is not the kind of workflow you can teach end-users. 
![screenshot_2018-09-29_11-30-22](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1318567/46249272-2a50e980-c3db-11e8-9f3b-72e9527a6581.png)

Is there a way to avoid these UI artefacts?

first things first: I am gratful beyond words for this package as it provides a huge amount of help in my work.

There is an annoying issue, which I am not able to fix. I have read a lot of forums and some (stackoverflow f.e.) offer some insights, as other users have encountered this issue as well. Anyway I could not implement a reliable solution and therefore decided to bring this question here.

I am building a shiny up, which uses many different instances of datatable to display various data. The user can interact with all of the data and they can modify, delete and add new records to the tables. The contents of the tables are saved in a reactive values. 

If I use the options settion according to point Nr. 2 on this link: https://rstudio.github.io/DT/options.html
everything works fine. I can set the desired page length and the table always renders as it should. I would like to achieve that the user may chose whatever page length settings she desires and keep this page length and page number settings after the table has been rerendered due to update of the reactive valueset behind the table. There are some similar questions on stackoverflow and I have tried all of the recommended solutions but nothing seems to be working for me.

My approach was:

- creating a variable for holding the prevously set user choices. 

`
### ---------- Shiny App Server Side Code ----------
server <- shinyServer(function(input, output,session) {
  
  #Workforce Table constants

 options = list(pageLength = if(is.null(workForcePoolOutput_previousPageLength)){10} else{workForcePoolOutput_previousPageLength},
 displayStart = if(is.null(workForcePoolOutput_previousPage)){0} else {workForcePoolOutput_previousPage},

`   #Observing the action button for new work force
    observeEvent(input$newWorkForceButton, {
    
    # Updating the holding variables of the previous table settings
    workForcePoolOutput_previousPageLength <<- input$workforcePoolOutput_state$length
    workForcePoolOutput_previousPage <<- input$workforcePoolOutput_rows_current[1] - 1
    
    #......... some function logic, works fine not related to the problem

    #updating the reactive value
    temp <- rbind(values$workForceData,new_fella)
    values$workForceData <- temp
    
    #Print the previous user setting for checking
    print(workForcePoolOutput_previousPage)

title: Table caption horizontal position
description:
Hi,

I'm using `DT`'s `datatable` for embedding tables in an `html` `Rmarkdown` document.

What I have is a list of `data.frame`s and I'm using this code so I can then simply embed all of the to the `html` output:


```
#create list
set.seed(1)
table.list <- lapply(1:3,function(i) data.frame(id = sample(LETTERS,3), val = rnorm(3)))
names(table.list) <- paste0("quite a long table name",1:3)

#loop over list and and concatenate the tables
table.out <- NULL
for(t in 1:length(table.list)){
  knit.expanded <- paste0("\n```{r results='asis', warning=FALSE,message=FALSE,echo=FALSE}\n\ndatatable(table.list[[", t, "]],rownames = FALSE,class='cell-border stripe',caption=names(table.list)[", t, "])\n\n```")
  table.out <- c(table.out,knit.expanded)
}

#Rmarkdown chunk to embed the tables
`r paste(knitr::knit(text = table.out,quiet=T), collapse = '\n')`
```


As you can see I'm embedding the names of the tables as captions and because these names are quite long they get cut off in the `html` output.

So my question is how to solve this?
Intuitively I thought there would be a parameter to specify the horizontal position of the caption. Since the captions are currently top and left centered, which is what's causing them to get cut off, I'd specify top center. But it seems that the only caption placing options in `datatable` are top and bottom.

Any idea?

title: selectRows(): after single row selection DT input does not register anymore
description:
Hi,
with the following example you can reproduce the bug. 
If an update is run on multiple rows the shiny input binding updates correctly and its registration is shown in the text element. 
But when updated only on a single row the input binding is lost and whatever you select is not registered.

# Example Shiny App
```rm(list = ls())
library(shiny)
library(DT)

runApp(
  launch.browser= T,
  shinyApp(
    ui = fluidPage(
      fluidRow(
        column(12,dataTableOutput('table'))
      ),
      fluidRow(
        column(
          width = 3,
          h5("Number of rows to select via selectRows():")
        ),
        column(
          width = 1,
          selectizeInput("nrowToUpdate", choices = 1:3, selected = 1, label = NULL)
        ),
        column(
          width = 1,
          actionButton("updateButton", "Update!")
        ),
        column(
          width = 4,
          h5("DT row selected input does not register only after selecting a single row via selectRows():")
        ),
        column(
          width = 3,
          textInput("selectedRows", label = NULL)
        )
      )
    ),
    server = function(input, output, session) {
      
      output$table <- renderDataTable(
        mtcars[1:10,],
        selection = 'multiple',
        extensions = c("Select")
      )
      
      DTproxy <- DT::dataTableProxy("table")
      
      observe({
        if (length(input$table_rows_selected) > 0)
        updateTextInput(
          session = session, 
          inputId = "selectedRows", 
          value = input$table_rows_selected
        )
      })
      
      observe({
        if (input$updateButton > 0)
        DT::selectRows(
          DTproxy,
          sample(1:10, isolate(input$nrowToUpdate))
        )
      })
      
    }
  )
)
```

title: `datatable` widget isn't anchored correctly to parent when used in `renderDataTable()`
description:
I usually encounter this issue in a `flexdashboard` document with `vertical_layout: fill`. 

When using `datatable()` _outside_ a reactive context, the `datatable` object will usually be anchored correctly to the parent widget. By that I mean that the `datatable` widget will be correctly scaled to fit the parent widget, and will be resized to fit the parent when the window is resized, etc. This makes the `datatable` widget always in sync with the parent, like this: 

    ---
    title: "MRE"
    author: ""
    output: 
      flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
        orientation: columns
        vertical_layout: fill
    runtime: shiny
    ---
    
    
    
    Page 1 {data-orientation=columns}
    =======================================================================
    
    Column {data-width=650}
    -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    ### Tab 1
    
    ```{r}
    # DT::renderDataTable({  ##uncomment to reproduce bug
        DT::datatable(mtcars, 
                      filter = 'top',
                      extensions = c('Scroller'),
                      options = list(scrollY=600, 
                                     scrollX=300, 
                                     scroller = TRUE,
                                     deferRender = TRUE,
                                     pageLength = 250))
    # })  ##uncomment to reproduce bug
    
    ```
    
    
    Column {data-width=650}
    -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    ### Tab 2
    
Here's how it renders in the app: 
![screenshot_2018-09-09_19-44-28](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1318567/45273735-d6508600-b468-11e8-8e6e-2cf8d79eb0ac.png)

Notice how the DT widget is sized so that it occupies all the available space within the tab. 

--------
Now uncomment the lines in the code above, so that the R chunk reads like this: 

    ```{r}
    DT::renderDataTable({  ##uncomment to reproduce bug
        DT::datatable(mtcars, 
                      filter = 'top',
                      extensions = c('Scroller'),
                      options = list(scrollY=600, 
                                     scrollX=300, 
                                     scroller = TRUE,
                                     deferRender = TRUE,
                                     pageLength = 250))
    })  ##uncomment to reproduce bug
    ```

Notice now how the DT widget is no longer in sync with the parent widget: however you resize the window, the widget is going to stay stuck at a fixed size. 
![screenshot_2018-09-09_19-56-20](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1318567/45274047-722ec180-b46a-11e8-8335-4134d60da88b.png)

This is problematic with end-users, since people use different screen resolutions, so for some the static widget size will be too small; while for others it will overflow the window -- like in the screenshot above -- and the horizontal scrollbars won't be visible, thus making it unusable, etc.

Is this an issue with DT? How can I work around this within a reactive context?

title: Consider removing noUiSlider dependency due to improper license
description:
Hi!

noUiSlider is licensed WTFPL, which is not considered a proper open source license. This it is a blocker to individuals within organizations to use and support this project:

https://opensource.google.com/docs/thirdparty/licenses/#wtfpl-not-allowed

This issues has been brought to the package maintainer on multiple instances. It doesn't look like it will be addressed there:

*  leongersen/noUiSlider/issues/885
*  leongersen/noUiSlider/issues/765

The fact that others can't use and work on WTFPL code goes against the spirit of being as open as possible. Please consider switching to a project that uses a different, permissive license, like Apache 2.0.

https://opensource.google.com/docs/thirdparty/licenses/#notice

Other similar projects, like crosstalk, use the ion rangeslider library. It would be an acceptable alternative here.

Thanks!
Michael

title: Multiple format*() functions on a column have no effect
description:
### Problem

Once the values of a column in a DataTable have been edited with a `format*()` function (e.g. `formatSignif()`, `formatString()`), any subsequent attempts to format the values of that column have no effect.

---

### System information

**OS:** Windows, RHEL6 and 7
**R:** 3.4.3
**DT:** 0.4 (CRAN), 0.4.12 (GitHub)

---

### Minimal example

```
library(DT)

dt <- datatable(iris[1:10, ])

# Significant figures edited correctly, but then not formatted as percentage
dt %>%
  formatSignif("Sepal.Length", digits = 1) %>%
  formatPercentage("Sepal.Length")


# Could have avoided that problem by using `digits` parameter of
# formatPercentage; but that might not always be possible...
dt %>%
  formatSignif("Sepal.Length", digits = 1) %>%
  formatString("Sepal.Length", suffix = " units")


# Even separating the steps does not help
dt2 <- formatSignif(dt, "Sepal.Length", digits = 1)
dt2 %>% formatString("Sepal.Length", suffix = "units")


# Style *is* applied as expected
dt %>%
  formatSignif("Sepal.Length", digits = 1) %>%
  formatStyle("Sepal.Length", backgroundColor = "cyan")
```

    iris, server = TRUE,
    filter = "top", 
    caption = 'colReorder + filter can have trouble',
    extensions = 'ColReorder',

title: resetPaging of replaceData() does not work with Scroller plug-in
description:
Hi, I have a data table (with the iris dataset) that uses the Scroller plug-in (scrollY). Users can change the  Sepal.Length value for a selected row after clicking on an actionButton. Im using `replaceData()` to refresh after the action.

Its working, but Im loosing the location of the change, it goes back to the beginning of the data table. Can I prevent this reset and save the Y position of the vertical scroll?.
I tried with resetPaging = FALSE but it does not work.

This is the fully operational example with the Iris dataset:

```
library(shiny)
library(DT)

ui <- fluidPage(
    fluidRow(
      column(2, 
             uiOutput("species_dropdown"),
             numericInput("value_select", "Sepal.Length Value:", value = 5, min = 1, max = 40, step = 1),
             actionButton('submit', 'Submit Change')
             ),
      column(10, DT::dataTableOutput('selectDT'))
    )
  )

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  ## LOAD DATA
  df <- iris

  ## SET DROPDOWN
  output$species_dropdown <- renderUI({
    selectInput("species_select", "Species Filter:", choices = c("All", levels(df$Species)), selected = "All")
  })

  ## REACTIVE DATA
  reactiveData <- reactive({
    input$submit
    req(input$species_select)
    data <- df
    # Filter rows
    if (input$species_select != "All") {
      data <- data[data$Species == input$species_select,]
    }
    data <- data
  }) # end reactive

  ## RENDER DT
  output$selectDT <- DT::renderDataTable(DT::datatable({reactiveData()}, 
                                                       selection = list(mode = "single", target = 'row', selected = previousSelection),
                                                       rownames = FALSE,
                                                       filter = 'bottom',
                                                       extensions = c('Scroller','Buttons'),
                                                       options = list(scrollX = TRUE,
                                                                      deferRender = TRUE,
                                                                      scrollY = 300,
                                                                      scroller = TRUE,
                                                                      paging = TRUE)),
                                         server = TRUE)
  ## GET SELECTED ROW
  previousSelection <- NULL
  selectedRow <- reactive({
    row <- input$selectDT_rows_selected
  })
  
  ## REFRESH DATA
  proxy = dataTableProxy("selectDT")
  # Observe click of "Submit Change" button
  observeEvent(input$submit, {
    # Save previously selected row
    previousSelection <<- input$selectDT_rows_selected
    # Change value of Sepal.Length in original data
    df[selectedRow(), ]$Sepal.Length <<- input$value_select

    # Replace data in proxy
    replaceData(proxy, reactiveData(), resetPaging = FALSE, clearSelection = "none")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```
Best,
Javier

title: Bootstrap styles overwritten
description: I discovered a perplexing error with the DT's Bootstrap styles. Here's a simple reproducible example with DT 0.4: ```R library(shiny) library(DT) ui <- function(request) { fluidPage( titlePanel("Test"), sidebarPanel( actionButton("load_table", "Load") ), mainPanel( DTOutput("faithful_table") ) ) } server <- function(input, output) { is_loaded <- reactiveVal(FALSE) observeEvent(input$load_table, { is_loaded(TRUE) }) output$faithful_table <- DT::renderDataTable({ if (!is_loaded()) return(NULL) datatable( faithful[1:20,], style = "bootstrap" ) }) } shinyApp(ui, server) ``` After clicking "Load", you get this: Instead of the expected result when you initially set `loaded` to `TRUE`: For the correct version, these assets are loaded in this order: ``` datatables-crosstalk.css datatables.js dataTables.bootstrap.min.css dataTables.bootstrap.extra.css jquery.dataTables.min.js dataTables.bootstrap.min.js ``` But when the table is loaded dynamically via the action button, you get this: ``` datatables-crosstalk.css datatables.js jquery.dataTables.min.css jquery.dataTables.extra.css jquery.dataTables.min.js dataTables.bootstrap.min.css dataTables.bootstrap.extra.css jquery.dataTables.min.js dataTables.bootstrap.min.js ``` It seems like what's happening is that DT doesn't know you're going to use Bootstrap style tables, so it loads the assets for the default theme even though they will never be needed. I was able to fix this particular example by changing `if (!is_loaded()) return(NULL)` to `req(is_loaded())`, but I'm sure a lot of people are still using the `return(NULL)` pattern. Furthermore, due to this same CSS incompatibility, you cannot mix Bootstrap and non-Bootstrap tables in the same app, as this test confirms: One possible solution would be to namespace the two different table styles, but I think a better solution would be to just make the table style a global option.

title: JSON object unnecessarily large for paged, server-side datatables; sends seq_len(DT)
description:
This is a feature request to prevent `dt_rows_all` being set to a vector that has one integer for each row in the entire table; instead it should be trimmed to match `dt_rows_current`. 

An unnecessarily large JSON object is sent over the network for very large, paged, server-side datatables. `DT_rows_all` is set to `seq_len(n)` (or some reordering), which is a very large vector, even though data is only sent for the rows in `DT_rows_current`. Indeed, for my application, which uses a 70K row table, the majority of the data sent over the network is `DT_rows_all`.

I would write a reproducible example, but it is clear that the authors are aware of this issue, it is marked as TODO in the code itself:

https://github.com/rstudio/DT/blob/116377810ec0acbbd8c693632ee5f03ac5a79371/R/shiny.R#L493-L502

I think, ideally, `DT_rows_all` would be set to `iCurrent`, which would make it redundant with `dt_rows_current`, but it would have less chance of breaking existing user code. It would also have to change here:

https://github.com/rstudio/DT/blob/a314d79c012e53adda2bf9119b34c4dc4da2379f/R/shiny.R#L399

Alternatively, the `filterFun` function in `sessionDataURL` function could be modified to trim `DT_rows_current` before encoding it as JSON.

Without changing the package at all, I could write a custom filter for large data tables, which would trim `dt_rows_all`. I'm not quite sure how to write a custom filter, and I couldn't find any examples. I saw the lack of examples referenced in issue https://github.com/rstudio/DT/issues/194 as well, perhaps this would be a good example to provide? Any quick tips would be very helpful as well.

I would be happy to provide a PR, but I wanted to get a sense of what strategy you think would work best for this (making `DT_rows_all` the same as `DT_rows_current`, or trimming it in `filterFun`).

description:
In a shiny app, when clicking a button to clear the selected rows by a simple `observeEvent`, using `selectRows(selected = NULL)` on a `dataTableProxy` throws this warning:

Using `selectRows(selected = list())` instead causes no warning, however the documentation of `dataTableProxy` says 
> ...you may use NULL to clear existing selections

It does work with `NULL`, but for me it results in a warning spam. Perhaps the documentation should be adjusted? I can provide more details of what I've done, but I think it's sufficient.

title: factor filters break when clicking outside the input box
description:
It looks like #319 was only partially fixed in `0.2`, and factor filters break down in some typical-usage circumstances. 

Try this: 
```{r}
library(shiny)
library(DT)

shinyApp(
    ui =
        fluidPage(
            DT::dataTableOutput("iris")
        ),
    
    server =
        shinyServer(function(input, output, session){
            output$iris <- 
                DT::renderDataTable({
                    datatable(
                        data = iris,
                        filter = "top",
                        options =

)

title: Can DT clear `rows_selected` after table is gone?
description:
I often use a `DT` table and rely on rows selected in the table to generate some relevant data. 

```r
# dt row selection after table gone
library(shiny)
library(DT)

ui <- fluidPage(fluidRow(actionButton("remove_table", "Remove Table"),
                         DT::dataTableOutput("table")) )
server <- function(input, output){
  value <- reactiveValues()
  value$dt <- cars
  output$table <- DT::renderDataTable({
    value$dt
  })
  observeEvent(input$remove_table, {
    value$dt <- NULL
    print(input$table_rows_selected)
  })
  observeEvent(input$table_rows_selected, {
    print(input$table_rows_selected)
  })
}
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

```

- If you click the `remove` button, the table data become `NULL` and is not displayed.
- However the selected rows data from `input$table_rows_selected` is left with previous values. You can click `remove` button again and again, and saw the values are still printed.

In my app sometimes I need to update some data dynamically, which caused the table data to first become `NULL`, then change to new values. There are some steps of changes because of multiple reactive values updating at the same time. Then the app will have this behavior:

- table is gone, but the rows selected value is still kept, which caused the code in app to apply those row index on a Null data frame and throw errors.
- table data updated, new table was shown, and the rows selected value is updated. The code above updated and get the correct result.
- so there will be a brief moment that `rows_selected` value cause error.

I have been able to work around this by using `freezeReactiveValue` on it. However I think it make sense to clear this value when the table is destroyed.

title: Feature Request: custom scaling and unit in formatting functions
description:
Hello there, before switching to DT, I've been using [formattable](https://renkun.me/formattable/) to format `data.table`s for presentation.

I think DT's formatting function are adequate for most purposes, but I find my self missing the `preproc` and `postproc` functions provided by `formattable()`. I use preproc when there is a need to change unit before displaying the value.

For example, I have a number `12345678901` and depending on the context, I may want to format it as `12,345,679K`, or `12,345.6M`, or `12.3B`, **and** still have it treated as a number instead of a string. The unit should not be limited to English either. For example Chinese read out numbers by an interval of 4, e.g. `12,345,67.9万元` etc.

With DT in mind, I don't think `preproc` and `postproc` would be necessary or easy. Instead I'm requesting that the formatting functions to have `scale` and `unit` parameters where as possible. Or perhaps `rescale` is more appropriate? Mock code:

```r 
datatable(data.frame(x = '12345.67') %>%
  formatNumber(
    'x', scale = 0.001, unit = 'k', digit = 1L)
# x is 12.3k
```

Update: I know that the `unit` thing can be hacked via `currency = 'k', before = FALSE` in `formatCurrency`. But I have yet to discover a way to rescale the data, short of modifying the original or creating a modified copy.

description:

```
library(shiny)

  DT::dataTableOutput("tab"),
  title = "example"

server <- function (input, output) {
  m = as.data.frame(round(matrix(rnorm(1000), 50), 5))

    m, extensions = 'FixedColumns',
    options = list(
      scrollX = TRUE,
      fixedColumns = list(leftColumns = 2, rightColumns = 1)

    print(input$tab_rows_selected)
