title: pattern for including htmlwidgets in datatable
description:
The examples for including `sparkline` and `d3horizonR` htmlwidgets in `DT` datatables received enough attention to motivate me to settle on a pattern for including nearly any htmlwidget in a datatable.  I will start by doing all in one pipeline and then break the steps down into functions with discussion below.

```

mtcars %>%
  group_by(cyl) %>%
  # step 1 summarise and convert htmlwidget to as character
  summarise(
    spk_line = HTML(
      as.character(
        as.tags(
          sparkline(hp, type = "bar")
        )
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  datatable(
    # step 2 make sure escape = FALSE
    escape = FALSE,
    # step 3 add code to render htmlwidget
    options = list(
      fnDrawCallback = htmlwidgets::JS('
function(){
  HTMLWidgets.staticRender();
}
')
    )
  ) %>%
  # step 4 add html dependencies for the htmlwidget
  tagList(
    htmlwidgets::getDependency("sparkline", "sparkline")
  ) %>%
  browsable()
```

### Step 1 - convert htmlwidget into character version

Hopefully, this piece will be eased with an official `as.character.htmlwidget` function in `htmwidgets`.

```r
as.character.htmlwidget <- function(x, ...) {
  htmltools::HTML(
    htmltools:::as.character.shiny.tag.list(
      htmlwidgets:::as.tags.htmlwidget(
        x
      ),
      ...
    )
  )
}
```

### Step 2 - make sure escape = FALSE

```r
datatable( ..., escape = FALSE )
```

### Step 3 - add static render callback

```r
add_datatable_render_code <- function(dtbl) {
  render_js_code = htmlwidgets::JS('function(){HTMLWidgets.staticRender();}')

  dtbl$x$options$fnDrawCallback <- render_js_code
  return(dtbl)
}
```



### Step 4 - add dependencies for the htmlwidget being used

```r
add_deps <- function(dtbl, name, pkg = name) {
  tagList(
    dtbl,
    htmlwidgets::getDependency(name, pkg)
  )
}
```

### Altogether now

```
library(htmltools)
library(htmlwidgets)
library(DT)
library(sparkline)
library(dplyr)

mtcars %>%
  group_by(cyl) %>%
  summarise(
    spk_line = as.character(
      sparkline(hp, type = "bar")
    )
  ) %>%
  datatable(escape=FALSE) %>%
  add_datatable_render_code() %>%
  add_deps("sparkline", "sparkline") %>%
  browsable()
```

title: Shiny rows_selected does not react to selectAll Button
description:
Hi,

It seems the shiny value input$...._rows_selected does not react to the selectAll button from the Select extension. Clicking the "Select All" button correctly selects the rows in the table, but the selection is not sent to Shiny. However, once unselecting a row, the rest of the selection is correctly sent to Shiny.

A minimal example:

```
library(shiny)
library(DT)

ui <- fluidPage(

  title = 'Select Table Rows',

  h1('A Server-side Table'),

  fluidRow(
    column(9, DT::dataTableOutput('x3')),
    column(3, verbatimTextOutput('x4'))
  )

)

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  # server-side processing
  mtcars2 = mtcars[, 1:8]
  output$x3 = DT::renderDataTable(datatable(mtcars2,options = list(dom = 'B',buttons=c("selectAll","selectNone")),extensions=c("Select","Buttons")), server = TRUE)

  # print the selected indices
  output$x4 = renderPrint({
    input$x1_rows_selected
    s = input$x3_rows_selected
    if (length(s)) {
      cat('These rows were selected:\n\n')
      cat(s, sep = ', ')
    }
  })

})
shinyApp(ui,server)
```

Thanks,

Andras

description:

```
library(shiny)
library(tibble)
library(DT)
dat <- tibble(Char = LETTERS, Factor = factor(LETTERS))
ui <- fluidPage(
  fluidRow(
    column(6L, 
           h3("server = TRUE"),
           dataTableOutput(outputId = "serverMode")),
    column(6L, 
           h3("server = FALSE"),
           dataTableOutput(outputId = "clientMode"))
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$serverMode <- renderDataTable(
    dat, server = TRUE
  )
  output$clientMode <- renderDataTable(
    dat, server = FALSE

}
runApp(appDir = shinyApp(ui, server))

title: Fix for Issue #265 breaks Shiny Superzip example.
Shiny app: single row selection doesn't work if server  = TRUE
description:
Shiny app: single row selection doesn't work if `server  = TRUE`

The issue appears when trying to use renderDataTable with with single row selection, e.g.

```
DT::renderDataTable(cars, selection = "single")
```

The default value for server is TRUE, so it's equivalent to

```
DT::renderDataTable(cars, server = TRUE, selection = "single")
```

When running the app graphically it looks fine, highlighting one row at the time. But intrinsically it behaves as with `selection = "multiple"` by adding subsequent row number values to `input$tableId_rows_selected` and removing them, if clicked for the second time.

![screen1](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/9052306/16983637/0eafd808-4e76-11e6-9fbc-a7de8be0cf16.png)

Once you skip to the next page of the table and then come back to the previous page, multiple selected rows are highlighted, but the highlighting disappears once you click a row. Interestingly, now you have to click twice on already selected rows to remove them from `input$tableId_rows_selected`.

![screen2](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/9052306/16983638/0eb27054-4e76-11e6-9a2d-2a0c4c85af26.png)

This behaviour is quite inconsistent and surely not intended for single row selection option.

Once use client side mode:

```
DT::renderDataTable(cars, server = FALSE, selection = "single")
```

everything works normal, single row number value gets updated in `input$tableId_rows_selected`. However, this imposes a kind of limitation, since as you say in doc, `server = FALSE` is not recommended for large data tables.

Below is the code to replicate the behaviour. Tested on Ubuntu/Windows, Firefox/Chrome/Rstudio

```
library(shiny)
library(DT)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  output$x1 = DT::renderDataTable(cars, server = FALSE, selection = "single")

  # client-side processing
  output$x2 = renderPrint({
    s = input$x1_rows_selected
    if (length(s)) {
      cat('These rows were selected:\n\n')
      cat(s, sep = ', ')
    }
  })

  output$x3 = DT::renderDataTable(cars, server = TRUE, selection = "single")

  # server-side processing
  output$x4 = renderPrint({
    s = input$x3_rows_selected
    if (length(s)) {
      cat('These rows were selected:\n\n')
      cat(s, sep = ', ')
    }
  })
}

ui <- fluidPage(

  title = 'Select Table Rows',

  h1('A Client-side Table'),

  fluidRow(
    column(9, DT::dataTableOutput('x1')),
    column(3, verbatimTextOutput('x2'))
  ),

  hr(),

  h1('A Server-side Table'),

  fluidRow(
    column(9, DT::dataTableOutput('x3')),
    column(3, verbatimTextOutput('x4'))
  )

)

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

title: Input$table_rows_all not working
description:
Hi,

I am using datatables in a shiny app. 
If I use the server side processing:

`output$printrules <- DT::renderDataTable(DT::datatable({
    rulesp()
  }, options = list(scrollX = TRUE, aLengthMenu = c(5, 10, 25, 50), iDisplayLength = 10)))`

[Server = TRUE](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-G-n_2SArytQ/VzyC51QQXgI/AAAAAAAAA3E/ro0YtAFKIsYTsDfCAWBzvI7H-k6_RJidwCLcB/s1600/server%253DTRUE.png)
It's all ok, but when I try to do input$printrules_rows_all it just prints the current rows.
I've read that rows_all isn't working on the server side processing. Then I switched to the client side processing:

`output$printrules <- DT::renderDataTable(DT::datatable({
    rulesp()
  }, options = list(scrollX = TRUE, aLengthMenu = c(5, 10, 25, 50), iDisplayLength = 10)), server=FALSE)`
(rulesp() is a reactive function that returns a dataframe)

And I am able to get the indexes of the rows. However the table is printed in a different way. The numbers become rounded and the table, somehow, gets messy. The 1.00000 become 1. And the spaces between columns become unformatted. [Server=FALSE](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-7faoW8APm_8/VzyC2g1j-WI/AAAAAAAAA3A/pRJcLscXCR4QAoGIhcleL0amGHHlpoqUwCLcB/s1600/server%253DFALSE.png)

This happens because the size of the columns vary. How to solve this? Is there a way to get the indexes in the server side processing? If not, how can I solve this strange behaviour?

Client side:
`DT::dataTableOutput("printrules")`

Thank's a lot!

title: Filter Issue
description:
Per discussion with RStudio Support:

Amanda Gadrow (RStudio Support)
May 4, 10:27

Nataraj,

I was able to reproduce your experience with this code:

```
library(shiny)
library(DT)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  employee = data.frame(
    `First name` = character(), `Last name` = character(), Position = character(),
    Office = character(), `Start date` = character(), Salary = numeric(),

})

I have filter = 'top' in the datatable definition, and when the app is run, I see the filter boxes, and I can enter text, but nothing happens when I execute the filter.

Could you please log your issue here: https://github.com/rstudio/DT/issues?  Please include a description of the problem and a code example, if possible, and the package maintainers can handle the issue directly.

Amanda

title: Problems with DataTables' Fixed Header Extension with {.tabset}

title: Set search field based on url parameter
Duplicate html widget name due to set.seed
description:
I had the problem of having the same table appearing twice. After looking at the md file I fould that the html widget id of the two tables was the same due to the setting of the same `set.seed()` as htmlwidgets::createWidget randomize the id name. My solution was to set another `set.seed` before `datatable` but wonders if there is any other better method. The reproducible Rmd file is below:

``````

---
title: "Untitled"
output: html_document

---

```{r}
set.seed(50)
numbers <- runif(10)
require(DT)
table1 <- data.frame(x = "1st table", value = numbers)
datatable(table1)
```

```{r}
set.seed(50)
numbers <- runif(10)
require(DT)
table2 <- data.frame(x = "2nd table", value = numbers)
datatable(table2)
# table 1 appears instead o table 2
```
``````

title: DT won't render within conditionalPanel
description:
Hello,

I've found that DataTables won't render within a conditionalPanel. Here is a reproducible example: 

``` r
library(shiny)
library(DT)
server <- function(input, output) {
  output$test <-DT::renderDataTable(mtcars)
  output$test1 <-DT::renderDataTable(mtcars)
}

ui <- fluidPage(
  sidebarPanel(
    textInput("bool","Enter anything")
  ),
  mainPanel(
    DT::dataTableOutput("test1"),
    conditionalPanel(condition='input.bool!=""',
                     h3("testing"),
                     DT::dataTableOutput("test")
    ))
)
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server) 
```

The first DataTable outside the conditionalPanel renders no problem. Then when you enter any text in the textInput, the conditionalPanel correctly opens since you can see the "testing" h3 text displayed, however the second DataTable is not rendered. Oddly enough, it works if you use the deprecated shiny version of DataTable:

``` r
library(shiny)
server <- function(input, output) {
  output$test <-shiny::renderDataTable(mtcars)
  output$test1 <-shiny::renderDataTable(mtcars)
}

ui <- fluidPage(
  sidebarPanel(
    textInput("bool","Enter anything")
  ),
  mainPanel(
    DT::dataTableOutput("test1"),
    conditionalPanel(condition='input.bool!=""',
                     h3("testing"),
                     shiny::dataTableOutput("test")
    ))
)
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server) 
```

This works totally fine, but I want to be able to use the `DT` package rather than the `shiny` version of `DT` because it has the `dataTableProxy`

Is this a bug or am I misunderstanding something?

```
[1] DT_0.1.45    shiny_0.13.1

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):

Kind Regards

title: using footerCallback to get multiple column sums
description:
Similar to issue #39 from a while back, I'm trying to get column sums in the footer of a DT. However, I'm trying to sum multiple columns in one go. I am trying to make use of `.columns().footer()` rather than `column().footer()`. The below code runs without error but the column sums are missing. Any suggestions?

Related to this is the column sum formatting: If I use `column( 1 ).footer()...` multiples times for each column, I get essentially what I want. However, I can't use `formatCurrency(..., '')` to get commas for the big numbers that result. How can I format these totals?

```
sketch <- tags$table(
    tableHeader(data),
    tags$tfoot(
      tags$tr(
        tags$th('Total'),
        tags$th(class='sum'),
        tags$th(class='sum'),
        tags$th(class='sum'),
        tags$th(class='sum'),
        tags$th(class='sum')
      )
    )
  )

  datatable(data, rownames = F, container = sketch, 
      options = list(
        dom = 't',
        footerCallback = JS(
          "function( tfoot, data, start, end, display ) {",

title: Better behavior with dynamically updating data sources
description: When used with reactive data sources, any updates to the data causes the pagination, selection, and filtering to be reset. It should be possible to not do that, at least when `server=TRUE`. Basically we should detect if the data argument is a reactive, and have an observer that detects changes to it and makes the client call [ajax.reload(NULL, FALSE)](https://datatables.net/reference/api/ajax.reload%28%29). title: Set targets in columnDefs dynamically
description: I use DT package to create a tool, allowing users to upload their own data and display it. I also use checkboxGroupInput() so users can choose which columns they want to display. Because the text contents in some columns are quite long, I use columnDefs in DT::renderDataTable() to restrict that the number of words to display is up to 20. The issue is that I found the targets arguments in columnDefs cannot be set dynamically. Suppose there is a data table with 10 columns. If I set "targets = c(1:10)", then it works fine, the definition in columnDefs will apply to all columns. However, if I set "target = c(1:length(input$columns))" where "columns" is the inputID of checkboxGroupInput(), then the format defined in columnDefs will be simply ignored. A strange behaviour I observed is that if I set targets to either "length(input$columns) - 1" or "c(1:(length(input$columns) - 1))", the format defined in columnDefs will apply to last column, dynamically. The problem of targets not able to set dynamically is that if the number of columns in user's data is less than the pre-defined range in targets, it will keep waiting the rest columns which do not exist. My code is as follows: ``` r server.R library(shiny) library(stringr) library(DT) shinyServer(function(input, output) { # "choose_columns": Check boxes output$choose_columns <- renderUI({ # If missing input, return to avoid error later in function if(is.null(input$inFile)) return() # Get the data set with the appropriate name inputFile <- input$inFile dat <- read.csv(inputFile$datapath, nrows = 10) colnames <- names(dat) # Create the checkboxes and select them all by default checkboxGroupInput("columns", "Choose columns", choices = colnames, selected = colnames) }) # "data_table": Output the data output$data_table <- DT::renderDataTable({ # If missing input, return to avoid error later in function if(is.null(input$inFile)) return() inputFile <- input$inFile # Get the data set dat <- read.csv(inputFile$datapath, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) # Make sure columns are correct for data set (when data set changes, the # columns will initially be for the previous data set) if (is.null(input$columns) || !(input$columns %in% names(dat))) return() # Keep the selected columns dat <- dat[, input$columns, drop = FALSE] }, options = list( columnDefs = list(list( targets = c(1:length(input$columns)), render = JS( "function(data, type, row, meta) {", "return type === 'display' && data.length > 20 ?", "'' + data.substr(0, 20) + '...' : data;", "}") )), searchHighlight = TRUE ), filter = "top", selection = list(mode = "single", target = "cell") ) # Render the content in selected cell output$text = renderText(input$data_table_cell_clicked$value) }) ``` ``` r ui.R library(shiny) shinyUI(pageWithSidebar( headerPanel(""), sidebarPanel( fileInput("inFile", "Choose datasheet to display"), uiOutput("choose_columns") ), mainPanel( verbatimTextOutput("text"), DT::dataTableOutput("data_table") ) )) ```

title: stateSave overides option parameters
description:
This is a follow up on #66, #76, and #77. I setup a repo with a minimal example to see if I can save and reset state for a DT table (see https://github.com/vnijs/dt_state). Column and global search work fine without `stateSave = TRUE`. The remaining parts (sorting, page, show) require `stateSave = TRUE`. 

My goals are to (1) maintain state, (2) restore state from a file, and (3) 'flush' state when needed.
1. Works seems to work well. It might be convenient to have an option `state` that can take an object with the same structure as `input$outputId_state` and parse it.
2. Seems to work only when starting up the app for the first time. However, if you refresh the browser `stateSave` stores its values and over-rides the parameters passed through options. To simulate what I'm looking for see line 15 in server.R. I would expect this value to be used on each refresh because it is passed to the `searchCols` option.
3. I haven't found a way to do this other than to close the browser. The refresh button/link doesn't work because `stateSave` overrides it.

The current `stateSave` setup probably works really well for client-side processing. However, for server-side processing it would be great if there was an option `state` that can take an object with the same structure as `input$outputId_state` and parse it. In my example I would assign this state to the r_state list that I can easily flush or I can load a new r_state from file and use that.

shinyServer(function(input,output,session){

 ) })

title: input$..._rows_selected not updated if row_id already present in the server side vector.
description:
I use a DataTable with the following parameters:

```
output$table <- renderDataTable({...},
                                     selection = 'single',
                                     server = TRUE)
```

when using input$table_rows_selected on the server side, it returns NULL, and then appends a vector of characters corresponding to the row names of the fist column, which happes to be called ID.

My workaround has been to use the equivalent of:

```
id <- input$table_rows_selected %>% as.character() %>% as.numeric()
id_current <- id[length(id)]
```

This gives me the currently selected row, by its database ID (in my application).

The server side input$table_rows_selected only updates if:
- A new column value (previously not included) is appended to the vector.
- The column value is deselected and re-selected, or before another is selected.

Is there a possibility to allow the server side input$table_rows_selected to update the vector even if a value is already present? Or alternatively, return only the current value?

title: Flexible formatStyle() - "target" and "condition" parameters?
description:
For somebody who has not worked in java script, I've found DT's helper functions to be a great benefit.  I just wanted to share my thoughts on making it more flexible.  Some of the common things I'd like to do are:  
- highlighting an entire row based on the value in one cell.
- highlight cells/rows based on rows or cells above and below 

I'm assuming I'm correct that I can't do this in the current implementation. There are probably reasons why the helpers are the way they are, but from the position of ignorant javascript bliss I imagine a formatStyle function that takes two arguments + styling
- target: the column names to which the formatting would be applied, and 
- condition: a logical vector of TRUE/FALSE corresponding to the rows of the table, indicating which rows to apply the formatting to

At that point, I would think one could have conditional formatting as complex as any logical vector you could construct?  Just my thoughts.  Thanks again for this great package.

title: The value of the datatable::rownames parameter affects 'target' indices
description:
I can understand why this is happening, but I think this is unintentional/undesired behavior.

A simple example is ordering the output on a particular column.

This:

```
datatable(mtcars, options=list(order=list(list(3, 'asc'))))
```

orders `mtcars` by its 3rd column (`disp`), but this:

```
datatable(mtcars, options=list(order=list(list(3, 'asc'))), rownames=FALSE)
```

will order it by its 4th column (`hp`)

Also, the `targets` values in `columnDefs` are equally affected, this centers `Sepal.Width`:

```
datatable(iris, options=list(
  columnDefs=list(
    list(className = 'dt-center', targets = 2)
  )))
```

and this centers `Petal.Length`

```
datatable(iris, rownames=FALSE, options=list(
  columnDefs=list(
    list(className = 'dt-center', targets = 2)
  )))
```

title: Fix sorting of columns in scientific notation
description:
These columns are parsed as characters in the output, and the sorting is hosed. A simple solution would be to use the [scientific sorting plugin](http://datatables.net/plug-ins/sorting/scientific) available from datatables.net.

An example is shown below. Try to sort on the `p` columns and you'll see what is the what:

``` r
p <- sprintf('%.2fe-%d',
             sample(seq(-1, 1, by=0.05), length(letters)),
             sample(1:10, length(letters), replace=TRUE))

df <- data.frame(name=letters, score=rnorm(letters), p=as.numeric(p))
datatable(df)
```

title: DT_RowId, or an approach to row selection info
description:
To be able to get the indices of selected rows, we need the id's of rows stored somewhere. DataTables accepts a field `DT_RowId` returned from the server data (http://www.datatables.net/examples/server_side/ids.html), but then we will have to use objects instead of arrays as the data source, which will be (slightly) more complicated. See https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/_1h6eStpr2U

An alternative (and IMO simpler) approach is to add the row id's as a column in the table, but do not display this column: http://datatables.net/reference/option/columns.visible Then users only need the data from this column to retrieve the selected rows from R.

title: Number formatters
description:
Provide simple R syntax so users do not need to write JavaScript to format numbers, e.g.

``` r
datatable(...) %>%
  format_col(c(1, 3), type = c('currency', 'percentage'), sep = c(',', ''), before = c('$', ''), after = c('', '%'))
# or column by column
datatable(...) %>%
  format_col(1, 'currency', sep = ',', before = '$') %>%
  format_col(3, 'percentage')
```
